title: SKAM (Norway)
description: The original Norwegian teen drama that started it all. Each season follows a different student at Hartvig Nissen school in Oslo, told with unusual realism and real-time episode drops. Season 3 follows Isak coming to terms with his sexuality.
notes: Where it all began! For me it's the best version — it's really sensitive and realistic. There are 4 seasons. Season 3 is the best one in my opinion (and it's also the gay season hehe). Season 4 is also <3 You can watch any season without having followed the others. I also love hearing Norwegian!

title: DRUCK (SKAM Germany)
description: The German remake of SKAM. Follows the same season-per-character structure but adds its own layers and plot twists, with a grittier tone.
notes: It has a slightly more depressing tone, but I love it, because it adds a different layer to season 3's main character, and they change things with a different plot twist (you'll understand). They're a bit more into drugs than the Norway kids, but well, it's Germany.

title: SKAM France
description: The French remake of SKAM, which eventually outgrew the original with many additional seasons. Season 3 (Lucas's season) is a fan favorite.
notes: This is possibly a lot of people's favorite. It's not mine, because it romanticizes the story a little too much, with a taste of French cinema sometimes. I only watched up to the middle of season 5 (yes, SKAM France outlasted the original).

title: SKAM Italia
description: The Italian remake of SKAM, known for its warm friend-group dynamics. Swaps the usual season order, telling the season 3 story in season 2.
notes: Nothing new added, but I love the dynamic between the friend groups, they're all adorable. It's a bit less depressing than the others — Latin country, warmer people heheh. The story that usually happens in season 3 happens in season 2 here. It was also good for brushing up my Italian.

title: wtFOCK (SKAM Belgium)
description: The Flemish-Belgian remake of SKAM, a faithful adaptation with strong performances.
notes: It's a good remake. I'm not suuuuper in love with it since it doesn't bring much new, but the performances kept me interested.

title: Bad Buddy
description: Thai BL series about Pran and Pat, next-door neighbors and lifelong rivals whose families hate each other — until life keeps throwing them together. Widely praised for subverting BL clichés with a healthy, tender love story.
notes: My favorite BL. It fully commits to the BL cliché, with every trope in existence (bad soundtrack, bizarre sound effects, a pretty cliché little story), but it manages to subvert the genre and show a super cute, healthy love story between two boys. They're two boys who've been neighbors since they were little, but whose parents hate each other. They're taught to hate each other growing up, but life happens and keeps throwing them together... hehehe The show gets SO GOOD from episode 4 on, so survive eps 1 and 2 (3 isn't bad). The good news: it's all on YouTube, complete and subtitled! Lesbian side couple!

title: A Tale of a Thousand Stars
description: Thai BL from the director of Bad Buddy. A heart-transplant recipient moves to a remote village to teach, honoring his donor's wish, and slowly falls for the local forest ranger chief. A gentle slow burn.
notes: Same director as Bad Buddy — perfeeeect, no complaints! It's about a boy who gets a heart transplant and a new life. He goes to live in a village in the middle of nowhere to be a teacher, just like his heart donor was. There he meets the chief forest ranger and they fall in love hehehehe Sounds silly, but it's really beautiful! And they're too cute! More of a slow burn. All on YouTube too, with subs!

title: I Told Sunset About You
description: Acclaimed Thai coming-of-age drama set in Phuket about two childhood friends reconnecting while studying for university entrance exams. Often compared to Call Me by Your Name; a landmark that pushed the whole BL industry forward.
notes: Simply THE drama of 2020 — it truly came to shake the structures of the BL industry in Thailand. Honestly, it steps way outside the BL mold. It has the same feeling as Call Me by Your Name, it's coming of age. Really beautiful and it makes you cry a little. But sooo good!

title: Until We Meet Again
description: Thai BL about two present-day students who are the reincarnations of a couple torn apart in the past. As red threads of fate pull them together, memories of their former lives resurface.
notes: My 2019 favorite. Two boys in the present day who are the reincarnation of another couple from the past. They meet and their souls recognize each other, and little by little they start remembering and understanding what's happening. The production isn't amazing and some of the acting leaves something to be desired, but I looooved the acting of two of them. The side couple has their own series: Between Us.

title: Not Me
description: Thai action drama directed by trans filmmaker and activist Anucha 'Nuchy' Boonyawatana. A twin returns from Russia to find his brother in a coma, takes his place among a gang of vigilantes to find out who hurt him — and falls for one of them. Rare BL that engages directly with LGBTQ+ and social justice issues.
notes: A classic. The revolutionary queers drama! A twin boy comes back to Thailand (he was living in Russia) and finds out his twin is in a coma. He decides to take his brother's place to find out who hurt him, ends up infiltrating his brother's friend group, and meets his future boy. They're vigilantes!!!! So many good moments! It's a rare series that talks about LGBTQ+ issues directly instead of just using them for clout. It had a low budget and barely any promotion, but a great turnout, because the leads are heavily shipped in Thailand heheh The director is a trans woman deeply engaged in the causes. There are action scenes (sometimes a little meh hehe). It has my favorite scene in any BL — I'll let you guess which one!

title: 2gether: The Series
description: One of the most popular Thai BLs ever: a student asks the campus heartthrob to fake-date him to ward off an admirer, and the pretend romance turns real. Followed by the shorter sequel Still 2gether.
notes: Fits more into the standard BL mold, but it's cute and the leads are hotties! Easy to watch hehe There's a sequel too, shorter and not as good.

title: Theory of Love
description: Thai BL about a film student hopelessly in love with his oblivious best friend, told through the lens of romantic movie theory. Frustrating in the middle, redeemed by the ending.
notes: Not my favorite, but it has its good moments. You spend a good part of the series angry, but I like the side couple and the ending. It has Gun Atthaphan, one of the best actors in Thai BL, twink extraordinaire. And his pair Off, who in this drama hadn't reached his acting potential yet (the next dramas are much better).

title: HIStory 2
description: Taiwanese BL anthology — one of the earliest and most polished BL franchises. Each story runs a few episodes, built on classic tropes executed well.
notes: Three stories told in a few episodes each. HIStory was one of the first BL initiatives and it's nicely made! Shorter series, but really good! The stories are based on kind of cliché tropes, but well executed. My favorites in HIStory 2 are the volleyball boys and the dad-and-the-babysitter one heheh

title: HIStory 3: Make Our Days Count
description: Taiwanese BL about a delinquent who falls for the class honor student. Sweet high-school romance with a devastating turn.
notes: Watch if you want to cry.

title: HIStory 3: Trapped
description: Taiwanese BL crime drama: a hot-headed police officer and a young gang leader get tangled up investigating a four-year-old case — and each other.
notes: Sooooo good! The gangster and the cop fall in love, that's it hehehe

title: We Best Love
description: Taiwanese BL two-parter (No. 1 For You and Fighting Mr. 2nd) about academic rivals whose one-sided rivalry hides something else entirely.
notes: Hate/love relationship, pretty well made! I enjoyed it. There's a second season: Fighting Mr. 2nd.

title: Cherry Magic
description: Japanese romcom: an office worker turns 30 as a virgin and magically gains the ability to hear the thoughts of anyone he touches — including his handsome coworker's very loud crush on him.
notes: The premise is suuuper silly, but the show is just too cuuute hahaha The main boy turns 30 and starts hearing other people's thoughts because he's still a virgin... yes. hahaha Japan, right? But it's nice.

title: Kieta Hatsukoi (My Love Mix-Up!)
description: Japanese high-school romcom built on a chain of adorable misunderstandings that starts with a borrowed eraser. Light, silly, and sweet.
notes: Same silly-but-cute vibe as Cherry Magic. Easy to watch.

title: Where Your Eyes Linger
description: One of Korea's first BL dramas: a chaebol heir and his bodyguard/childhood best friend navigate feelings neither is allowed to have. Short and sweet.
notes: Korea is only now entering the BL world... they still have a lot of progress to make hehe. A boy and his bodyguard (who is also his childhood friend). Cute and short.

title: Semantic Error
description: Korean campus BL: a rigid computer science major and the free-spirited design senior whose graduation he accidentally ruined. Opposites attract, chaos ensues. One of Korea's biggest BL hits.
notes: The last one I watched. College drama. Cute, short and easy to watch.

title: Color Rush
description: Korean BL with a fantasy twist: in a world where some people see only greyscale, a 'mono' meets the one person who makes him see color. Available as both a series and a movie cut.
notes: There's a movie version and a series version. It's cute, nothing wooow.

title: Gameboys
description: Filipino BL filmed entirely during (and set in) the pandemic lockdown, told through video calls. A gamer falls for the fan who challenged him online. Surprisingly moving.
notes: It was filmed during lockdown! And it's set during lockdown! It was really touching at the time, I cried. It's very cute — sometimes it focuses a little too much on the emotions.

title: Pearl Next Door
description: Gameboys spin-off centered on Pearl, a bi protagonist caught between two women. One of very few GL (girls' love) series out there.
notes: Finally a lesbian series! (actually the protagonist is bi). Honestly I didn't love this one, because the girl she likes at the beginning is awful and she's torn between two — I don't really enjoy love triangles 😭 buuuut, I like the protagonist. (It's a Gameboys spin-off.) I watched it ages ago and haven't watched many GL series since.

title: Hello Stranger
description: Filipino BL, also filmed in quarantine: a jock and a nerd are forced to partner on a class project over video calls. Has a follow-up movie.
notes: Also filmed in quarantine times. It's cute — sometimes a little too dramatic hehe There's a movie too!

title: Heartstopper
description: Netflix adaptation of Alice Oseman's beloved webcomic/graphic novels: schoolboys Charlie and Nick fall for each other in the softest, most joyful queer coming-of-age story on TV.
notes: I like the first season. It's too goody-goody and not realistic enough for me sometimes.

title: Shelter
description: Indie drama about a young artist in a California surf town torn between family obligations and a romance with his best friend's older brother. A quiet, tender classic of 2000s queer cinema.
notes: Possibly one of my favorites, because I used to watch it with my best friend who passed away in 2013. It's sweet and sensitive. It's hard to find on the internet — there's this low-quality one on YouTube.

title: Everybody's Talking About Jamie
description: Film adaptation of the West End musical about a Sheffield teenager who dreams of becoming a drag queen — and wants to attend prom in a dress.
notes: Such a good movie! Not my favorite musical, but the film is really well made and the lead actor puts on a show. It's about a teenager who wants to become a drag queen.

title: Latter Days
description: Low-budget cult romance between a closeted Mormon missionary and his party-boy neighbor in LA, wrestling with the clash between sexuality and faith.
notes: These old movies we find on YouTube. This one is veeeery low budget. But it's nice. The story of two neighbors in LA — one of them is a Mormon missionary and the other is pretty promiscuous. About that conflict between sexuality and religion.

title: The Boys in the Band
description: Netflix adaptation of Mart Crowley's landmark 1968 play (produced by Ryan Murphy): a birthday party among gay friends in 1970s New York unravels over one sharp-tongued evening. Great script and performances.
notes: Based on the play of the same name. I love the rhythm and the script, and the performances are quite good. Some parts are hard to understand, since a lot of the content is cultural references from that era, I think. But it's really good. A slice of life of gay friends in the '70s. It's on Netflix.

title: Daddy
description: Short film starring Dylan Sprouse exploring an unconventional relationship dynamic.
notes: It's a short film with Dylan Sprouse. It's interesting.

title: But I'm a Cheerleader
description: Cult satirical comedy: a cheerleader's parents ship her off to a conversion-therapy camp, where she promptly falls for another girl. Campy, colorful, and iconic.
notes: A classic! It's very campy and funny! Her parents send her to an anti-gay camp, but she falls for one of the girls hehe

title: Trashy LGBTQ+ Christmas Movies (list)
description: Paste Magazine's roundup of the glorious new genre of trashy-but-queer Christmas movies.
notes: GAY CHRISTMAS — this article has a list of movies from this new genre I love: trashy Christmas movies, but make it LGBTQ+.

title: Moonlight Chicken
description: Jim runs a late-night chicken rice diner in Pattaya; one closing time, Wen stays past last call. A grounded, melancholy slice of life about money, grief, and chosen family — with one of BL's best deaf-character storylines. First, Khaotung, Earth and Mix all in one show.
notes: Really good, but much more realistic and down-to-earth. From my favorite director. It has my 4 favorite Thai actors. Sometimes it's a little too depressing, but so good.

title: We Are
description: A sprawling GMMTV university ensemble: a big friend group, most of them gay, falling for each other across 16 easygoing episodes.
notes: A really silly series and way too long, but for some reason it's one of those shows I put on in the background while doing other things. It's too long because everything is already resolved by the halfway point. And there are like 15 boys, most of them gay. Not very realistic, but it has its cute moments.

title: Perfect 10 Liners
description: Basically three seasons in one: 24 episodes following three university couples (8 episodes each) who all exist in the same world.
notes: Also a silly one, but it's basically 3 seasons in 1. It has 24 episodes, but we follow 3 couples — each couple gets 8 episodes. They all know each other and exist in the same world. The first couple is ok but boring. The second is ok but one of the guys annoys me, and the third couple is the best and healthiest <3

title: The Eclipse
description: At a strictly governed all-boys school, a rumored curse punishes students who step out of line — until a new transfer student starts questioning everything. School drama wrapping a real message about authoritarianism and protest. First and Khaotung's first series together.
notes: The first series with my favorite actors together — First and Khaotung. The message is good, but it's delivered through a high school drama that's sometimes hard to take seriously. Still, their acting and the chemistry between them make it totally worth it.

title: The Heart Killers
description: An irreverent Taming of the Shrew adaptation (with plenty of 10 Things I Hate About You references): two brothers raised as assassins by their adoptive mother, and the two men hired to woo them. Raw, stylish, and carried by a killer soundtrack.
notes: Another one with my favorite actors. It's a very irreverent adaptation of Shakespeare's 'The Taming of the Shrew', with lots of references to 10 Things I Hate About You (an adaptation of the same play). Katarina and Bianca are two brothers who were adopted by a woman who taught them to be assassins. Great adaptation, and as is typical of this director, it's pretty raw. There's one boy whose acting is really bad, hard to ignore sometimes. The soundtrack is incredible and it's what made me discover Thai metal 😆

title: Only Friends
description: The show about the messy gays: a group of hospitality students running a hostel project while hooking up, lying, and self-destructing. No BL tropes, no perfect boys — everyone is nuanced, flawed, and human.
notes: The show about the messy gays. It's great. Everyone is nuanced and not perfect. This is what I love about P'Jojo's shows, he doesn't lean into the BL tropes and clichés. He also tends to work with the good actors.

title: Between Us
description: Spin-off of Until We Meet Again following fan-favorite side couple Win and Team: the secret friends-with-benefits relationship that ran alongside the first series, now shown in full.
notes: The audience's favorite couple from Until We Meet Again. In this series we see the development of the friends-with-benefits relationship of UWMA's side couple in the same timeline — which we didn't see in detail in the first series, since their relationship is a secret. It has good moments, but there was so much hype and it took so long to come out that it disappointed me a bit. Some moments of very exaggerated acting. But I really like the characters, so if you watched UWMA and liked them too, it's nice.

title: Wandee Goodday
description: A med student gets rejected and stumbles into a friends-with-benefits deal with a sunshine boxer. Nothing revolutionary — just two charming actors with great chemistry having a very good time.
notes: Very underrated. Friends with benefits with two guys who act well and are sexy. I like it a lot. Nothing revolutionary, but really fun and cute.

title: Last Twilight
description: Day, a former badminton player losing his sight, meets Mhok, his unusual new caretaker — and slowly learns to live his new life. A nuanced, mostly non-cliché take on disability (with a finale that split the fandom).
notes: A very well done show about a boy who becomes blind and how meeting his new unusual caretaker helps him accept his situation and learn to live his new life. I find that it is nuanced and brings in some not-so-cliché takes on disability, even though there are clichés. The only reason it's not a 5 star is the last episode, which divided opinions in the fandom. I still don't know how to feel about it.

title: Cherry Magic Thailand
description: Thai remake of the Japanese hit, starring TayNew: turn 30 a virgin, gain mind-reading powers, discover your coworker adores you. Due to rights issues GMMTV couldn't upload this one to YouTube internationally — it streams on Viu.
notes: I think I enjoyed it more than the Japanese version. I like Tay Tawan and the secondary couple. Junior is a great actor.

title: My School President
description: Student council president Tinn has a hopeless crush on Gun, leader of the school's struggling music club. The debut of GeminiFourth, one of Thailand's most beloved pairs — sweet, teen, and full of band songs.
notes: The first drama of one of Thailand's most famous pairs: Fourth and Gemini. It's a silly teen series, but I enjoyed their band's songs. It's the favorite drama of everyone who was 12 to 16 when it came out. Fourth is an actor with so much charisma — it's nice to see him already shining in his first project.

title: Me and Thee
description: An ex-mafia heir turned perfume CEO ropes an introverted photographer into being his love coach — then pursues him instead, in world-record-setting ways. A comedy openly making fun of the mafia genre, lakorns, and BL itself. The sequel, Peach and Me, is ongoing.
notes: So funny. It's very cringe at times, sometimes on purpose, sometimes not. But I love the idea. It's a show that's making fun of the Mafia genre, but also of Lakhorns and BLs (Thai dramas). Some of the acting still needs to be worked on, but Pond is great in comedy. Peach and Me is the sequel and it's ongoing.

title: Bed Friend
description: Thai BL about two roommates and best friends who agree to become 'bed friends' with no strings attached — until real feelings complicate the deal.

title: Boys Be Brave!
description: Korean BL about roommates in a share house whose easy friendship tips into something more.

title: Cooking Crush: Uncut Version
description: Thai BL set in a cooking-competition show, where two rival contestants' kitchen sparks turn romantic.

title: Cutie Pie
description: Thai BL about a shy, awkward boy paired up with the school's popular playboy in an arranged 'dating' setup by their families.

title: Dark Blue Kiss
description: Thai BL sequel to Dark Blue Kiss's parent series (Kiss Me Again), following an aspiring makeup artist and a stoic, tattooed college senior.

title: Enchanté
description: Thai BL about a warmhearted magic-shop worker and a jaded, wealthy bookstore heir who keep crossing paths.

title: Fish upon the Sky
description: Thai BL: a university freshman develops a one-sided crush on an older engineering student he keeps mistaking messages for, and it slowly grows mutual.

title: Hidden Agenda
description: Thai drama-thriller where a man investigating his brother's death goes undercover and gets tangled up with a queer love interest along the way.

title: I Cannot Reach You
description: Japanese BL where two former college friends, one of them grieving, reconnect years later and slowly rebuild an emotional bond.

title: Individual Circumstances
description: Korean BL webseries about two men navigating a slow-burn romance shaped by their very different personal circumstances.

title: Jun & Jun
description: Korean BL following two men who share the same nickname 'Jun' and gradually fall for each other.

title: Love Sea
description: Thai BL revolving around a seaside town love story between two young men, part of the GMMTV lineup.

title: Love Tractor
description: Korean BL (also known as A Tractor Loaded with Love) set in a rural town, about two men whose paths cross over farm life and unexpected romance.

title: Lovely Writer
description: Thai BL about a novelist who bases his BL story's rude-boy character on a real actor he clashes with — then has to work with him for the adaptation.

title: Mr. Heart
description: Korean BL anthology-style short series centered on tender, everyday queer romance.

title: My Love Mix-Up! (Thailand)
description: Thai remake of the Japanese school romcom Kieta Hatsukoi, about a chain of mistaken-identity crushes sparked by a borrowed eraser.

title: My Only 12%
description: Thai BL where a man discovers a secret 12% stake his late father left him in a company — tangled up with the CEO's son.

title: Naughty Babe
description: Thai BL about mismatched roommates — one uptight, one carefree — whose bickering turns into something else.

title: Only Boo!
description: Thai BL GMMTV series about two men navigating an exclusivity ('only you') pact that turns into real feelings.

title: Our Skyy 2
description: GMMTV anthology sequel revisiting couples from past Thai BLs (2gether, Theory of Love, and others) in new bonus storylines.

title: Roommates of Poongduck 304
description: Korean BL about four university roommates sharing a flat, following the romance that blooms between two of them.

title: SOTUS
description: Landmark Thai BL about a rebellious freshman and the strict senior in charge of hazing him during university orientation — enemies who slowly fall for each other.

title: SOTUS S
description: Sequel to SOTUS, following the established couple as they navigate a public relationship, family pressure, and senior year.

title: Step by Step
description: Thai BL about two men whose long friendship is tested and deepened as they take their relationship step by step.

title: The Eighth Sense
description: Korean BL webseries where a man who can sense danger keeps being pulled toward someone who might be trouble — in more ways than one.

title: This Love Doesn't Have Long Beans
description: Thai BL comedy about a chaotic love story that keeps hitting absurd obstacles — the title's running joke.

title: To My Star Season 2: Our Untold Stories
description: Second season of the Korean BL about a star chef and the actor he's fallen for, deepening their relationship after the first season's slow burn.

title: Unintentional Love Story
description: Korean BL about a webtoon writer and his editor whose professional relationship turns into an unplanned romance.

title: Vice Versa
description: Thai body-swap BL/fantasy comedy: two people from different eras end up switching bodies and lives, love included.

title: Why R U?
description: Korean remake of the Thai BL Why R U?: The Series, about two students, one popular, one bullied, who end up entangled after an accidental video leak.
